selected_mechanism.definition: A rulemaking petition gate is the step where a state agency must answer a public request for a new rule by denying it in writing or opening a formal rulemaking within 60 days.
selected_mechanism.texas_scope: Public Utility Commission of Texas, Project No. 60084, a petition about metering large data center computational loads on the Texas electric grid

layers.function: Lets an interested person ask a state agency to adopt a rule and starts a 60 day clock on the agency.
layers.actor_authority: Government Code Section 2001.021 gives interested persons the petition right and binds the agency to deny in writing or initiate rulemaking within 60 days.

chokepoint.post_decision_phrase: deny the petition in writing or initiate a rulemaking proceeding
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: The statute makes the agency answer within 60 days with only two lawful outcomes, and the Commission order is the signed act that picks one. Staff recommend, petitioners and commenters argue, but neither controls the decision.

selected_mechanism.texas_consequence: A petition asking the Commission to adopt a measurement standard for computing inside large data centers, described in the staff memo as particularly those running high-intensity AI workloads, did not become a rulemaking. The order says the Commission's Senate Bill 6 rulemaking slate in Project No. 58317 is already full and contains no express or implied requirement to meter transport-layer consumption or computational efficiency. This record does not show the internal metering proposal proceeding in any other project.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The gate converts an open ended public request into a dated binary answer with written reasons. Here the order rested on existing Senate Bill 6 rulemaking workload and staff resources, and the staff memo added that the petition lacked usable rule text under Section 22.281 and that nothing in Senate Bill 6 requires metering inside individual data centers. The record shows the gate worked as a legible deadline. It does not show the internal metering proposal proceeding in any other Commission project, and it does not assess the merits of metering.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: A narrower petition with complete proposed rule text would be an observable route to a formal answer. The fetched record does not identify another project where this proposal proceeds.

next_check.what: Staff presentation of a proposal for publication of a standard large load interconnection agreement, which the September 2026 Senate Bill 6 roadmap in Project No. 58317 says staff anticipates in October 2026. The roadmap does not mention this petition.
next_check.actor: Public Utility Commission of Texas staff and Commission

evidence_gaps: No independent news corroboration of the October 1st order was found in two searches, so the trigger rests on the Commission's own filing.
Section 22.281 text was verified through the Texas Register adoption preamble, not the codified rule page, which was not reachable.
Staff memos give different dates for the project reassignment, so the post omits that date.
Signature block legibility limits confirming how many commissioners signed, so the post says the Commission without a vote count.

The record does not show the internal metering proposal proceeding in any other Commission project. An earlier draft inferred that Project No. 58317 now carries it. The order says the opposite, that the slate contains no requirement to meter transport-layer consumption or computational efficiency, so that inference was removed.
selected_mechanism.history_comparison: Not one of the prior six mechanisms (Taylor cooling-water exception framework, TCDC power-to-equity framework, TCEQ data-center permit pause, PGRR144 as-built model review, Batch Zero Verification RFI process, NSF Science and Technology Center cooperative agreement). It is an agency procedure gate, not a grid study or permit.
selected_mechanism.neutrality_screen: Covers authority, deadline, procedure and stated reasons only. The petition and supportive comments contain advocacy language, which is not adopted. No position is taken on metering, data centers or the petitioner.

required_post_phrases: deny the petition in writing or initiate a rulemaking proceeding

verified_facts.claim: Government Code Section 2001.021(c) requires a state agency, not later than the 60th day after submission of a petition, to deny the petition in writing stating its reasons or initiate a rulemaking proceeding.
Section 2001.021(a) lets an interested person petition a state agency to request adoption of a rule.

Under Section 22.281, a rulemaking petition must include a brief explanation, each reason, the statutory authority and complete proposed text, and a noncompliant suggestion is construed as a policy recommendation.
Green Recursive Utility Service LLC filed a petition for rulemaking on August 3rd, 2026 asking for a measurement standard for large computational loads.
Commission staff set a comment deadline of September 11th, 2026 in Project No. 60084.
The Commission received 74 comments in support of the petition.
Oncor Electric Delivery Company filed comments taking no position on the legality, merits or need for the relief requested.
The staff memo dated September 25th, 2026 recommended denial and described the petition as seeking metering of large data centers, particularly those running high-intensity AI workloads.

The staff memo said the petition did not include complete rule text as required by Section 22.281(a)(1) and that nothing in Senate Bill 6 requires the Commission to meter or regulate the internal computational activities of individual data centers.
The order states the Commission must deny the petition in writing or initiate a rulemaking proceeding by October 2nd, 2026.

The order dated October 1st, 2026 denied the petition, the revised petition and any other requested relief. It states the Commission already has a full slate of Senate Bill 6 rulemaking projects, per the SB6 Implementation Roadmap filed in Project No. 58317, that do not include an express or implied requirement to meter and regulate transport-layer consumption or computational efficiency of large load customers, and that initiating the requested rulemaking would require redirecting staff resources.
The petition and supporting comments were filed in Project No. 60084 and the staff memo is addressed to the Commission chairman and commissioners from the Rules and Projects Division Director.
Neither the fetched order nor the fetched staff memo identifies another project in which the internal metering proposal proceeds.

The September 22nd, 2026 SB6 Implementation Roadmap in Project No. 58317 says staff anticipates presenting a proposal for publication of a standard large load interconnection agreement for Commission consideration in October 2026.
The fetched roadmap text does not mention Project No. 60084 or a project to measure computing inside data centers.
